key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr offered the best overall wear–corrosion performance, while HVOF achieved the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-exposed stainless steel components, HVAF is a strong coating candidate, with process selection guided by service conditions.
method: Deposited WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation, HVOF and HVAF spraying.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, volumetric wear rate and corrosion behavior.
Examined wear tracks to identify abrasive and fatigue wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF achieved a wear rate of (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for uncoated steel, and the lowest reported coating corrosion current density, 1.75±0.02 µA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion electrolyte, limiting direct extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
